comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C3, C14-C18 regarding MIC data and synergy of the triple combination. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED with similar reasoning about comprehensive data and appropriate controls.

Both address claims C19-C22 on time-kill curves. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, while peer review shows UNCERTAIN due to initial methodological concerns about interpretation, though later marked as adequately addressed.
Perfect agreement on claims C23-C29, C46-C48 regarding membrane disruption. Both rate SUPPORTED and highlight the strength of using complementary techniques (fluorescence assays and SEM).
Perfect agreement on claims C30-C32 regarding selective PMF disruption. Both rate SUPPORTED and note the selective effect on Δψ component with appropriate fluorescent probes.
Perfect agreement on claims C33-C37 regarding ROS generation. Both rate SUPPORTED and accept the ROS mechanism as part of comprehensive investigation without challenge.
Perfect agreement on claims C38-C40, C70-C73 regarding CheA downregulation and chemotaxis. Both rate SUPPORTED and note the strength of overexpression validation experiments.

Both address ABC transporter claims C74, C80-C81. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED noting appropriate negative interpretation. Peer review also SUPPORTED, accepting the transcriptome findings without challenge.
Both address SpvD claims C82, C85-C86. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with modest effect noted. Peer review also SUPPORTED, accepting overexpression validation as part of comprehensive methodology.

Both address MCR-1 inhibition claims C99-C104. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to speculative mechanism and need for direct biochemical evidence. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, accepting molecular docking and competitive inhibition data as sound methodology.
Perfect agreement on claims C44-C45 regarding in vivo efficacy. Both rate SUPPORTED, with peer review highlighting in vivo validation as a strength. OpenEval notes modest effect size as limitation.

Perfect agreement on claims C49-C51 regarding LPS targeting. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights good experimental design with controls; peer review accepts as supporting evidence for membrane damage mechanism.
Perfect agreement on claims C41-C43, C53, C58, C61 regarding metabolome data. Both rate SUPPORTED and accept the low transcriptome-metabolome correlation as appropriately noted.

OpenEval rates claims C52-C57 on prostaglandin mechanisms as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative nature and lack of direct causal demonstration. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mechanistic claims.

OpenEval rates claims C59-C65 on antimicrobial compound accumulation as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of functional validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific metabolite mechanism claims.

Both address mcr-1-independent synergy claims C87-C88. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to speculative mechanistic interpretation. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, explicitly affirming the finding applies to both MCR+ and MCR- strains.

Both address toxicity claims C106-C110 (OpenEval includes C105). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED noting appropriate caution about limitations. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN with explicit concerns about nephrotoxicity of triple combination not adequately discussed.
OpenEval rates summary conclusions C111-C113 as SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these summary claims.
Peer review rates background claims C1-C2, C7-C13 as SUPPORTED, providing established context. OpenEval did not produce a separate evaluation for these background/contextual claims.
